Chapter 9: The Journey of Faith—Trusting the Unseen Path.
You know, a lot of people think faith means having all the answers—like you’re supposed to be certain and never doubt. But let’s be honest, for most of us, faith feels more like trying to find your way in the dark. You take a step, not really sure what’s ahead, and you just hope the path will show up as you go.
There’s this story I love—a student once told their mentor how scared they were about the future. The mentor just smiled and started talking about crossing a river at night. Picture it: the bridge is covered in thick fog, and you can barely see anything but your next couple of steps. But here’s the thing—with every step you take, more of the bridge comes into view. The mentor said, “Faith isn’t about seeing the whole path. It’s just about taking the next step.” Isn’t that such a relief?
In Eastern traditions, faith is really about trust. It’s about letting go of that need to control every little detail and just surrendering to the flow of life. The Taoist sage, for example, puts their trust in the Tao—even when it makes no sense at all. And Christ, well, he invited his followers to trust in God’s love, even when everything felt uncertain.
Most of us, if we’re honest, crave guarantees. We want to know everything will turn out all right. But life just doesn’t work that way, does it? The real invitation is to trust—to believe that, even when we can’t see what’s coming, there’s something, or someone, guiding and sustaining us.
There’s another story that comes to mind. A couple was stuck, agonizing over a tough decision. They analyzed every option, asked for advice, even prayed for a sign. But in the end, there wasn’t a perfect answer waiting for them—just the next step. So they chose to move forward, one small step at a time, trusting that they’d find the path as they walked.
Here’s something to remember: faith isn’t about never doubting. It’s about having the courage to keep moving, even in the middle of all that uncertainty. It’s risking, it’s hoping, and it’s believing that, somehow, something good can come out of the messiest situations.
In a lot of Asian traditions, the journey itself is more important than the destination. The path is sacred. Every twist, every unexpected moment, whether it’s joyful or confusing, is a chance to learn and grow. Christ didn’t promise a life of certainty—he invited us to a life of trust, to follow, even when the way ahead is blurry.
I’ll never forget the story of a traveler lost in a foreign city. They asked a stranger for help, but couldn’t speak the same language. Through gestures, smiles, and a bit of patience, they ended up finding the way together. The journey took longer than expected, but it turned into an adventure. That’s faith—not having all the answers, but being willing to walk alongside someone else and discover the way together.
So, if you’re feeling lost or unsure, know this: the journey of faith is never a straight line. There will be doubts, surprises, and moments of awe. But it’s always worth taking—a journey that leads to deeper trust, greater love, and a richer experience of the mystery of Christ.
